summary: Concentric rings, one for each agent, each filled to its share of that agent's own target, so agents with very different targets sit side by side. The middle shows the overall share, or the agent you point at. Every value is printed in the legend as done / target, a ring past its target goes round again with a marker where it ends, and a Week and Month switch changes the period.
use: To show how several agents (or teams, or goals) are doing against targets of different sizes.
On a weekly review where the question is who is on target and who is behind.
When people need the exact numbers as well as the picture.
features: A thick ring per goal, outermost first, in the chart palette, on a grey track. Three goals read best; the rings share the space between the edge and the readout, so the more goals there are, the thinner each ring.
Past its target a ring goes round again from the top, its end cutting into the ring under it (in Soft) with a small marker on it, and its share shows as a green tag ("110%").
The middle shows the average share across the goals, or the share of the goal you point at, counting to the new value.
Legend rows print each goal's done / target with its unit and its share.
Pointing at a ring or a row, or moving the focus to a row, lights both and dims the other rings.
An optional range switch (`ranges`, `range`, `onRangeChange`), and a line under the title that says how many are on target.
a11y: Each legend row can take the focus and has a label with the numbers, like "Research agent: 18 of 24 reports, 75% of target".
A visually hidden table carries every goal, its done and target values and its share, with the title as its caption.
The rings are hidden from screen readers, since the rows and the table hold the same numbers.
Values are always printed, so nothing depends on telling the ring colours apart.

faq.a: Two to five, and three read best. The rings share one band between the edge and the readout in the middle, so three are 14 units thick, four are about 10 and five are 7; more than five would be too thin to read.

faq.q: How is the overall share worked out?
faq.a: It is the average of each goal's share, so a goal past its target can lift the average above another's shortfall.

faq.q: Can I leave out the range switch?
faq.a: Yes. Leave out `ranges`, or `onRangeChange`, and the header shows the title and its line only.
